features.text: The patient is 65 years old and male.
The patient has experienced shortness of breath for about a week, primarily when walking, especially up stairs or when walking quickly.
The patient has swelling in both legs.
The patient had foot pain in one foot, specifically in front of the big toe, which was treated with Motrin and resolved after a few days.
The patient does not have chest pain, palpitations, or fever in the past week.
The patient has a history of coronary disease, including a heart attack in 2018 and a stent in the right coronary artery.
The patient has a low ejection fraction of about 35%.
The patient has stage three chronic kidney disease.
The patient takes Lasix, 40 mg once a day.
The patient has no allergies.
The patient does not know if there is a family history of relevant conditions.
The patient's blood pressure has been around 135/80 recently.
The patient has been taking Lasix as prescribed.
The patient has not noticed any changes in the color or temperature of their legs.
The patient has not had any changes in urine output, and there is no nausea, vomiting, or abdominal discomfort.
The patient has stage three chronic kidney disease, as confirmed by a kidney function test a month ago.
The patient has not had any recent changes in heart symptoms, and has not had an echocardiogram or recent follow-up with their cardiologist.
The patient has not had any recent changes in urine output, and there is no nausea, vomiting, or abdominal discomfort.
The patient has not experienced any new or worsening chest pain, palpitations, or dizziness in the past week.
The patient has not had any recent blood tests for uric acid, C-reactive protein (CRP), or erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR).
The patient has not had any recent episodes of joint pain or stiffness.
